memory.content: GBrain sync recipe: pull with `delta` using a stable session_id, loop while has_more, dedupe by fact_id (at-least-once delivery); push only new knowledge via `remember` (entity, content_origin, provenance, batches of up to 20, fresh UUID request_id reused only on retry, branch on inserted/duplicate/superseded); correct with `replaces`, not forget+new; skip own echoes; `context_pack` at session start; `synthesize` rarely (costs money). skills.name: gbrain-getting-started
skills.description: Use for the first conversation with a new owner of a GBrain sync bot, to set up the connection and routines.
skills.content:
---
name: gbrain-getting-started
description: >-
  Use for the first conversation with a new owner of a GBrain sync bot, to set
  up the connection and routines.
---
I keep your Grok Bot memory in sync with GBrain (github.com/garrytan/gbrain) and help you run it.

Ask these one at a time, using a widget where options are clear, and skip anything already known:
1. Do you use hosted gbrain.io or your own self-hosted server?
2. Check whether a GBrain connector is already connected and ready. If not, ask for the MCP URL (hosted: the gbrain.io MCP URL; self-hosted: https://<host>/mcp, often a Tailscale URL from `gbrain mcp expose`), add it, and run its auth card.
3. Self-hosted only: is storage PGLite or Postgres/Supabase? Is a jobs worker running (`gbrain jobs supervisor`)? Does the nightly cycle run (`gbrain dream` / `gbrain autopilot`)? How many jobs show as waiting in Jobs Watch?
4. Do other agents already write to GBrain? (So I don't duplicate their writes.)
5. Should I set up the routines: an hourly two-way sync on weekdays during working hours, a weekday morning health check that alerts only on problems, and a Monday report? Mention that they can run around the clock instead.

With the answers: save the installation type, URL host, engine and other writers as profile memory; create the routines the owner agreed to, in their own timezone; run a read-only test (delta plus recall) and report the result in one line. If jobs are waiting or consolidation is backed up, give the exact server-side commands (`gbrain doctor --json`, `gbrain jobs stats`, `gbrain jobs supervisor start --detach`, `gbrain dream`).

routines.name: GBrain hourly sync
routines.description: Fires hourly on weekdays to keep Grok Bot memory and GBrain in two-way sync.
routines.content:
Sync Grok Bot memory with the owner's GBrain (gbrain memory connector). Pull: fetch changes since the last run using a stable session id (gbrain-grokbot-sync) and keep paging until nothing more remains. Dedupe by fact id, and save the facts that genuinely matter to all assistants into shared memory, skipping ones already there. Push: write to GBrain only new durable facts learned in Grok Bot memory since the last run that aren't in GBrain yet. Set entity, content origin and provenance on each, use a fresh request id per write (reuse it only on retry), and correct facts by superseding them rather than forgetting them. Skip echoes of my own writes and anything other syncing agents already wrote. Never forget facts in bulk. Results go to the owner in this Grok Bot chat, but only when something fails or needs their action; a run with nothing to report stays silent.

Fires on:
- cron `40 9-18 * * 1-5`

Ask the importing user for:
- Timezone

routines.name: GBrain morning health check
routines.description: Fires each weekday morning to catch GBrain connector, sync, or backlog problems.
routines.content:
Health-check the owner's GBrain through its memory connector. Confirm the connector responds and that sync worked over the last day, and record the facts-pending-consolidation count in my journal so I can see the trend. If the connector fails, sync is stale, or the pending count has grown since the last check, tell the owner what's wrong and the exact server-side commands to run (for example `gbrain doctor --json`, `gbrain jobs stats`, `gbrain jobs supervisor start --detach`, `gbrain dream`). Results go to the owner in this Grok Bot chat only when something is wrong; a healthy run stays silent.

Fires on:
- cron `10 8 * * 1-5`

Ask the importing user for:
- Timezone

routines.name: GBrain weekly report
routines.description: Fires every Monday to summarize the week's GBrain sync and any server work due.
routines.content:
Write the owner a short weekly GBrain report covering the past week: roughly how many facts I pulled and pushed, how the facts-pending-consolidation backlog changed (from my journal notes), any sync failures, and any server-side commands they should run (jobs worker, nightly cycle, upgrades, backups via `gbrain export` or Postgres dumps). Keep it to a few sentences. The report goes to the owner in this Grok Bot chat every Monday, even when it's a quiet week.

Fires on:
- cron `10 9 * * 1`

Ask the importing user for:
- Timezone
